USAID DISINFORMATION RESEARCH PARTNERS IN UKRAINE AND THE REGION (5/11/22)
Please find below a list of the Ukraine Mission's partners that are conducting research on
disinformation in Ukraine and the broader region.
1. Ukraine World is NGO Internews Ukraine's topical news and information resource
focusing on Ukrainian issues which brings together around 300 experts and journalists
from Ukraine and around the world. They do regular explainers and analysis of
Russian disinformation trends in the Ukrainian infosphere.
2. Detector Media is a Ukrainian NGO focusing on democratic media development,
media reforms and combating propaganda, as well as a media watchdog carrying out
reviews, in-depth analysis and critical assessments of Ukrainian TV and radio content,
and current Ukrainian media trends. Detector Media collects and documents Kremlin
disinformation around Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
3. Texty.org is a data journalism agency which focuses on studying Russian propaganda
and disinformation in the media. Texty.org developed a browser add-on called
"Fakecrunch" for Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox which allows users to report
disinformation. Texty also produces regular analysis of Russian disinformation trends.
4. VoxCheck is a fact-checking project that monitors and verifies the statements of
politicians and opinion leaders.
5. Institute of Mass Information is a Ukrainian NGO that monitors and reports on media
trends and developments in Ukraine (with a special focus on online national and
regional media), publishing a Barometer of Free Speech, reports on ethical and
professional media standards, Russian narratives, propaganda and fakes in Ukrainian
online media, reports on gender balance, hate speech, national minorities and LGBTI
coverage in media. IMI manages the Media Inclusion List: monitoring media and
producing a list of those that perform best according to professional media standards,
and therefore safe places for advertisers to promote their brands.
6. Center for Democracy and Rule of Law is a think and act tank that supports the
creation of a good legal operating environment for developing independent media,
public platforms, and movements. It develops and advocates for quality legislation,
protecting freedom of speech, and providing impartial legal expert evaluation and
advice for journalists and media companies.
7. Independent Media Council is a public advisory and expert body designed to promote
high professional standards of journalism and self-regulation in the Ukrainian media
sector by providing expert opinions. The Council considers controversial issues
regarding non-compliance with media legislation, international standards of media
coverage, as well as violations of journalistic ethics.
8. Center for Analytics and Investigations launched the fact-checking project Bez
Brekhni (Without a Lie) examining politicians' statements, and specializing in
conducting fact-checking trainings. It created the first Ukrainian rating of Politicians'
Truths and Lies.
